name: Google Calendar
description: Events and calendars in Google Calendar.

objects.label: events
objects.description: Meetings, appointments and all-day events on one calendar. Google lists events one calendar at a time.

fields.label: guest
fields.description: A person invited to the event.

fields.label: response
fields.description: How the calendar owner answered the invitation.

objects.label: calendars
objects.description: The calendars the account can see, including shared and subscribed ones.

fields.label: hidden
fields.description: Not shown in the calendar list.

actions.label: an event
actions.description: One event per record. Guests get an invitation unless the builder turns notifications off.

params.label: starting at the time in
params.description: The source field that holds the date and time.

params.label: on the calendar
params.description: Leave blank for the account's primary calendar.

actions.label: a time block
actions.description: A busy block with no guests, for example prep time before each meeting or a slot per task.

params.label: on the calendar
params.description: Leave blank for the account's primary calendar.

actions.label: guests
actions.description: Invite the people in the source to an existing event. The source must hold people or email addresses.

guidance: Google Calendar is reached through the Calendar API, normally as a service account with domain-wide delegation acting as a named user, or with each calendar shared directly to the service account's address. Every read and write names a calendar: a person's own is called primary, and shared calendars are addressed by an id the owner copies from calendar settings. Creating an event with guests sends invitations straight away, so prefer writing to a dedicated automation calendar people subscribe to over inviting them one by one.

setup.notes: Ask the Google Workspace administrator for a service account, then have each calendar's owner share it with the service account's address at the access level the plan needs.
